# Docs

Shared notes for every game in this repository. Game-specific notes stay in each game's `AGENTS.md` and its own
docs folder. Start with `AGENTS.md` at the root; it says which of these to read before each kind of work.

## Techniques

- [game-notes.md](game-notes.md): proven techniques for proving changes, rendering, art direction, multiplayer,
  input, feel and audio. Read before rendering, performance, input, multiplayer or feel work; add an entry once a
  technique is proven.
- [netcode.md](netcode.md): how Arcade games hide network latency (client prediction, `OptimisticEvents`, wind-ups,
  adaptive time-stretched `SnapshotBuffer`, `hermite2` + coasting + `Glide`, `RewindHistory`, `RollbackClient`,
  `socketJitter`, and the new-game checklist). Read before any multiplayer or net work.
- [rendering-techniques.md](rendering-techniques.md): catalogue of rendering techniques with have/missing status,
  cost and location. Read before adding lighting, shadows, materials, post-processing or GPU performance work.
- [animation.md](animation.md): rules and measured values for procedural human animation (gait, contacts, arms,
  posture, transitions, weapons) and the known gaps. Read before touching any character's motion.
- [audio-design.md](audio-design.md): the shared audio engine and Audio Lab. Read before changing game sound.
- [sfx-library.md](sfx-library.md): the shared sound library (semantic ids, variants, licences, loudness targets),
  its offline generation and curation pipeline, and Outbreak's positional sound. Read before adding or replacing a
  sound; [sfx-inventory.md](sfx-inventory.md) measures every sound file in the repository.

## Shared code and conventions

- [prototyping.md](prototyping.md): the toy-first workflow (`bun scripts/new-toy.ts <name>`): how to prove game feel
  on `@arcade/kit` primitives and `LabPanel` knobs before building custom meshes, shaders or multiplayer rooms.
- [shared-code.md](shared-code.md): what the games still duplicate and what belongs in `packages/kit/`. Check
  before writing something another game already has.
- [human-rig.md](human-rig.md): API and module ownership of the shared human rig, profiles, attachments,
  detachment and the Characters page. Read before using the rig in a game.
- [controls.md](controls.md): cross-game key bindings and HUD prompts. Read before changing input or prompts.
- [architecture.md](architecture.md): the current engine map (layers, `@arcade/kit` and `@arcade/knobs` areas,
  generated per-game shared-module adoption table, core patterns, and staged roadmap). Read before a cross-game
  refactor.

## Lab and showing Kit

- [lab.md](lab.md): the Lab authoring contract for tunable effects, materials, physics, audio and rendering
  options. Read before adding or tuning any of them.
- [lab-workbench.md](lab-workbench.md): the current Lab shell and its input API.
- [lab-adapters.md](lab-adapters.md): how a game adds Lab sections, material and physics adapters, and spawnables.
- [knobs-requests.md](knobs-requests.md): what Arcade has asked knobs for, and whether a sync has brought it yet.
- [lab-effects.md](lab-effects.md): how to tune Blackout and Getaway effects in the Lab.
- [lab-scenes.md](lab-scenes.md): proposal for focused labs, lab kinds and collections (AR-25), and its data-model spike.
- [dev-control.md](dev-control.md): the `arcade` CLI for driving Kit's open browser tab, tours and pinned notes.
- [dev-hub.md](dev-hub.md): the local Dev Hub that serves every game from one origin.

## Releases and game plans

- [agent-state.md](agent-state.md): live deploy/branch policy (`deploys: on|off`, `allowed_base`, `retired_branches`),
  proof defaults, preview worktree rules, and hot-file contention rules enforced by `scripts/agent-ops.ts` and `pr-guard.yml`.
- [integration.md](integration.md): how to assemble and verify a release integration branch, and the past release
  PRs. Read before merging several feature branches together.
- [zomboid-slice.md](zomboid-slice.md): the plan for Outbreak's co-op survival game.
- [outbreak-coop.md](outbreak-coop.md): how Outbreak's 2–4 player co-op works (rooms, prediction, snapshots) and
  what it measured. Read before changing `shared/coop-sim.ts`, the room or `@arcade/kit/net`.
- [outbreak-world.md](outbreak-world.md): how Outbreak's procedural world generation, chunk streaming, districts,
  POIs, incremental bakes and chunk deltas work.
- [outbreak-progression.md](outbreak-progression.md): Outbreak's inventory (hotbar, the case and bags, containers, drops)
  and the safehouse workbench, built on the `@arcade/kit/sim/ledger` store-and-rule engine. Read before changing
  items, loot, crafting or `shared/progression.ts`.
- [outbreak-way-out.md](outbreak-way-out.md): The Way Out (AR-64), Outbreak's win condition: a hidden seeded
  destination found through clues, a signal, a stand until dawn and the escape card. Read before changing
  `shared/way-out/` or how a run ends.
- [outbreak-interactions.md](outbreak-interactions.md): world interactions (AR-96): throwables (baseballs, bricks,
  rocks, cans, bottles with a wound-up arc), what interactions already existed, and how each is taught. Read before
  adding a way to act on the world.
- [outbreak-difficulty.md](outbreak-difficulty.md): the difficulty-ramp playtest (survivor bots, per-hour probe,
  banded test in `bun run check`, full batch with charts) and how to update its bands. Read before tuning difficulty.
- [outbreak-discovery.md](outbreak-discovery.md): D-19 "Discovered, Not Told": state read from the world instead of
  labels (beam, boards, open containers), and how the squad learns recipes. Read before adding HUD text or recipes.
- [outbreak-strategy.md](outbreak-strategy.md): co-op strategy (AR-99, D-45): what makes survival co-op strategic
  in other games and six ranked systems for Outbreak. Read before adding team mechanics, specials or roles.
- [outbreak-secrets.md](outbreak-secrets.md): the town's unstated backstory and its secrets in three tiers (subtle,
  strange, hidden), with the cellar chain's solution. Spoilers. Read before adding lore, easter eggs or world details.
- [outbreak-onboarding.md](outbreak-onboarding.md): the training room (AR-89): Ash at dawn, wordless beats, skip and
  persistence, solo only.
- [outbreak-hud.md](outbreak-hud.md): Outbreak's character HUD, what other games put on the character, and the defaults.
- [outbreak-map.md](outbreak-map.md): Outbreak's map (N): what it shows, its input, the optional compass ring and
  minimap, and how per-chunk memory and cached tiles keep it cheap in a streamed world.
- [outbreak-art-direction.md](outbreak-art-direction.md): Outbreak's shipped look (Darkwood v8): rules, targets by
  hour, the flashlight spec, what not to do and how to prove a change. Read before touching its shaders, lighting
  or look settings.
- [outbreak-look.md](outbreak-look.md), [outbreak-look-v2.md](outbreak-look-v2.md): Outbreak's look studies.
- [style-playground.md](style-playground.md): the 9-style rendering playground on Outbreak's room sim, measured GPU costs, and full-game scaling verdicts.
- [outbreak-zombie-profile.md](outbreak-zombie-profile.md): Outbreak's zombie art controls on the shared rig.

## Agent skills

- [`procedural-animation-iteration`](../.opencode/skills/procedural-animation-iteration/SKILL.md): the
  measure-first loop and scripts for tuning character animation.

/**
 * Special zombies: which kinds exist, how rare each is and when, and their stats. Pure data and pure functions, so the
 * client (silhouettes, sounds) and the sim share one table.
 *
 * A zombie's kind lives in its seed: a special's seed carries the kind in its low four bits and a 12-bit check in its
 * top bits (`encodeSpecialSeed`), so the kind reaches co-op clients through the seed the wire already sends and needs
 * no new field. An ordinary seed passes the check about once in 11 000 zombies; the sim flips a check bit on those.
 */

export const SPECIAL_NONE = 0
export const SPECIAL_RUNNER = 1
export const SPECIAL_BRUTE = 2
export const SPECIAL_SCREAMER = 3
export const SPECIAL_BLOATER = 4
export const SPECIAL_RIOT = 5
export const SPECIAL_LURKER = 6

export type SpecialKind = 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5 | 6
export const SPECIAL_KIND_IDS = ["runner", "brute", "screamer", "bloater", "riot", "lurker"] as const
export type SpecialKindId = (typeof SPECIAL_KIND_IDS)[number]

/** Where a kind may appear and when. `night`: only once it is dark. */
export type SpecialRule = {
  readonly id: SpecialKindId
  readonly kind: Exclude<SpecialKind, 0>
  readonly label: string
  /** How a player spots it, and the answer to it (Lab tooltips, docs). */
  readonly read: string
  readonly counter: string
  readonly phase: "any" | "night"
  /** `street`: wherever zombies spawn; `police`: near a police station or cruiser; `dark-room`: moved into an unlit room. */
  readonly placement: "street" | "police" | "dark-room"
}

export const SPECIAL_RULES: readonly SpecialRule[] = [

    id: "riot",

    counter: "Front is armoured and shoves bounce off; flank it or hit its back",
    phase: "any",
    placement: "police",
  },
  {
    id: "lurker",
    kind: SPECIAL_LURKER,
    label: "Lurker",
    read: "Black clothes, crouched still in an unlit room",
    counter: "Your light wakes it: check rooms with the light off, or be ready",
    phase: "any",
    placement: "dark-room",
  },
]

export function specialRule(kind: SpecialKind): SpecialRule | undefined {
  return kind === SPECIAL_NONE ? undefined : SPECIAL_RULES[kind - 1]
}

export function specialKindFromId(id: string): SpecialKind {
  const i = SPECIAL_KIND_IDS.indexOf(id as SpecialKindId)
  return i < 0 ? SPECIAL_NONE : ((i + 1) as SpecialKind)
}

/** Rarity, phase ramp and stats. Flat numbers so the session tuning and the Lab panel carry them as they are. */
export type SpecialsTuning = {
  /** 1: specials appear. 0: every zombie is ordinary. */
  specialsOn: number
  /** Multiplies every chance below. */
  specialRate: number
  /** Chance that a zombie appearing by day is special, on the first day. */
  specialDayChance: number
  /** Chance that a zombie appearing at night is special, on the first night. */
  specialNightChance: number
  /** Added to both chances for every night after the first. */
  specialRampPerNight: number
  /** The chance never passes this. */
  specialMaxChance: number
  /** Relative weights among the kinds allowed at that moment and place. */
  runnerWeight: number
  bruteWeight: number
  screamerWeight: number
  bloaterWeight: number
  riotWeight: number
  lurkerWeight: number
  /** Riot cops within this distance of a police station or cruiser; elsewhere their weight is scaled by `riotStray`. */
  riotPoliceRadius: number
  riotStray: number
  /** Runner: health, speed when chasing at night (× the zombie's own), and by day. */
  runnerHp: number
  runnerSprint: number
  runnerDaySpeed: number
  /** Brute: health, speed, how much faster it beats down barricades and doors. */
  bruteHp: number
  bruteSpeed: number
  bruteBash: number
  /** Screamer: health, shriek wind-up (s), shriek loudness (noise radius, m), cooldown (s). */
  screamerHp: number
  shriekTime: number
  shriekRadius: number
  shriekCooldown: number
  /** Bloater: health, speed, gas cloud radius (m), how long it hangs (s), damage per second to survivors and zombies. */
  bloaterHp: number
  bloaterSpeed: number
  gasRadius: number
  gasTime: number
  gasDamage: number
  gasZombieDamage: number
  /** How much of a step a zombie keeps inside the gas (0..1), and stamina a survivor loses per second in it. */
  gasSlow: number
  gasStamina: number
  /** Riot cop: health, frontal arc (degrees either side of facing), damage let through from the front. */
  riotHp: number
  riotArc: number
  riotFront: number
  /** Lurker: health, speed once awake, and how close a survivor can stand before it wakes in the dark (m). */
  lurkerHp: number
  lurkerSpeed: number
  lurkerWakeNear: number
  /** A room counts as dark below this light level (0..1.5; an unlit interior at night is ~0.12, by day ~0.47). */
  lurkerDark: number
}

export function specialsTuning(resolved?: { features?: Readonly<Record<string, Record<string, unknown>>> }): SpecialsTuning {
  const src = resolved?.features?.specials as Partial<SpecialsTuning> | undefined
  return src ? { ...DEFAULT_SPECIALS_TUNING, ...src } : DEFAULT_SPECIALS_TUNING
}

export function specialWeight(t: SpecialsTuning, kind: SpecialKind): number {
  switch (kind) {
    case SPECIAL_RUNNER:
      return t.runnerWeight
    case SPECIAL_BRUTE:
      return t.bruteWeight
    case SPECIAL_SCREAMER:
      return t.screamerWeight
    case SPECIAL_BLOATER:
      return t.bloaterWeight
    case SPECIAL_RIOT:
      return t.riotWeight
    case SPECIAL_LURKER:
      return t.lurkerWeight
    default:
      return 0
  }
}

/** Where the world stands when a zombie appears: how dark (0..1) and which night it is (0 before the first). */
export type SpecialPhase = { darkness: number; night: number }

/** Chance that a zombie appearing now is special. */
export function specialChance(t: SpecialsTuning, phase: SpecialPhase): number {
  if (t.specialsOn <= 0) return 0
  const d = Math.max(0, Math.min(1, phase.darkness))
  const base = t.specialDayChance + (t.specialNightChance - t.specialDayChance) * d
  const ramp = t.specialRampPerNight * Math.max(0, phase.night - 1)
  return Math.max(0, Math.min(t.specialMaxChance, base + ramp) * Math.max(0, t.specialRate))
}

/** Whether `kind` may appear now: Runners only after dark. */
export function specialAllowed(kind: SpecialKind, phase: SpecialPhase): boolean {
  const rule = specialRule(kind)
  if (!rule) return false
  return rule.phase === "any" || phase.darkness >= 0.5
}

/** 32-bit mix (murmur3 finaliser). */
export function mix32(h: number): number {
  h = Math.imul(h ^ (h >>> 16), 0x85ebca6b)
  h = Math.imul(h ^ (h >>> 13), 0xc2b2ae35)
  return (h ^ (h >>> 16)) >>> 0
}

/** A zombie's two independent rolls, from the town seed, its id and its seed: [is it special, which kind]. */
export function specialRolls(townSeed: number, id: number, seed: number): [number, number] {
  const a = mix32((townSeed ^ Math.imul(id + 0x51, 0x9e3779b1) ^ mix32(seed)) >>> 0)
  const b = mix32((a ^ 0x2545f491) >>> 0)
  return [a / 4294967296, b / 4294967296]
}

/**
 * Picks a kind from `weights` (index = kind - 1) with the uniform roll `u`, or `SPECIAL_NONE` when every weight is 0.
 */
export function pickSpecialKind(weights: readonly number[], u: number): SpecialKind {
  let total = 0
  for (const w of weights) total += Math.max(0, w)
  if (total <= 0) return SPECIAL_NONE
  let r = u * total
  for (let i = 0; i < weights.length; i++) {
    const w = Math.max(0, weights[i]!)
    if (r < w) return (i + 1) as SpecialKind
    r -= w
  }
  for (let i = weights.length - 1; i >= 0; i--) if (weights[i]! > 0) return (i + 1) as SpecialKind
  return SPECIAL_NONE
}

const CHECK_SHIFT = 20
const LOW_MASK = 0xfffff

function seedCheck(low: number): number {
  return mix32((low ^ 0x5bd1e995) >>> 0) & 0xfff
}

/** The seed a zombie of `kind` carries: its own seed's middle bits, the kind in the low nibble and a check on top. */
export function encodeSpecialSeed(seed: number, kind: Exclude<SpecialKind, 0>): number {
  const low = ((seed & 0xffff0) | kind) & LOW_MASK
  return ((seedCheck(low) << CHECK_SHIFT) | low) >>> 0
}

/** A zombie's kind, read from its seed (0 for an ordinary zombie). */
export function specialKindOf(seed: number): SpecialKind {
  const s = seed >>> 0
  const k = s & 0xf
  if (k < SPECIAL_RUNNER || k > SPECIAL_LURKER) return SPECIAL_NONE
  return s >>> CHECK_SHIFT === seedCheck(s & LOW_MASK) ? (k as SpecialKind) : SPECIAL_NONE
}

/** An ordinary seed that happens to read as special, with one check bit flipped so it no longer does. */
export function ordinarySeed(seed: number): number {
  return specialKindOf(seed) === SPECIAL_NONE ? seed >>> 0 : (seed ^ (1 << CHECK_SHIFT)) >>> 0
}

/** Whether a hit from `(fromX, fromY)` lands on the front of a zombie at `(x, y)` facing `aim`, within `arcDeg`. */
export function hitFromFront(x: number, y: number, aim: number, fromX: number, fromY: number, arcDeg: number): boolean {
  const dx = fromX - x
  const dy = fromY - y
  if (dx * dx + dy * dy < 1e-8) return true
  let d = Math.atan2(dy, dx) - aim
  d = Math.atan2(Math.sin(d), Math.cos(d))
  return Math.abs(d) <= (arcDeg * Math.PI) / 180
}

# Outbreak world interactions (AR-96)

Kit, after the co-op playtest: "Also maybe like baseballs you can throw? The ability to drag items. Or board up
windows? More world interactions..."

Code: `games/outbreak/shared/interactions/` (rules, one shared feature `interactions`) and
`games/outbreak/src/interactions/` (drawing, hint, Lab, staging). Lab: Backquote › Interactions; every interaction is
on by default and its "Today (off)" is one setting away. Station: `outbreak-interactions` (`arcade station
outbreak-interactions`). Command: `arcade cmd interactions.stage scene=baseball|can|bottle|brick`.

## What was already there

Before AR-96 the world already had: doors (E open/close, hold E lock, keyed doors unlocked with a key or pried with a
crowbar, Shift+E peephole), windows (E peek or climb, hold E open/close), fence vaults, barricades (B nails one plank
on the door or window the prompt points at, three at most, reinforced with the toolbox recipe, re-nailed with a
crowbar, worn by the dead with the bowed/hanging plank look), containers (E search, Shift+E smash), closets (hide),
can tripwires (strung with Mouse0, disarmed and re-strung with E), abandoned cars (E smash a window, alarms), bottles
(Mouse0, a fixed 12 m throw that breaks into glass), noisemakers, road flares, the fire kit (flamethrower, dynamite,
firecrackers, molotov, flare gun, bear trap), Lights Out lamps, radios, searchable bodies, chained dogs (food), the
Way Out's parts, gas cans, hotwiring and roadblocks, the Recipe Board (C or E at a bench), downed survivors revived
with hold E, G drop and hold G bundle, and Q ping. AR-96 extends these rather than adding parallel versions.

## Throwables

Baseballs, bricks, rocks, tin cans and bottles. Bottles are the old item, now thrown the new way.

- **Found** lying about: 70% of houses (Lab › Throwable houses) have one, seeded from the town alone
  (`toss-sites.ts`): a brick, rock, baseball or can by the front door or in the yard, or a can, baseball or bottle on
  a floor beside a table or counter. They are `drop:v:yard:<building>` ground drops, picked up with E like any drop,
  put out once per house (one taken never comes back). Bottles are still in containers as before.
- **Throw**: hold Mouse0 with one in hand. The arc (beads) and a ring where it comes down are drawn while you wind
  up, and the ring turns red when the throw will hit one of the dead. Release to throw: a tap throws 30% of full range
  (Lab › Tap throw), a full wind-up (0.75 s) the whole of it. A press with nothing held (bots, a click inside one
  frame) throws at full strength.
- **Flight**: a long lob flies over the heads of the dead in the middle and can hit one only near either end, so a
  can lobbed over a crowd lands behind it. A throw stops at walls, shut doors, boarded windows and abandoned cars and
  falls back; on open ground it hops and rolls. A brick, rock or baseball goes through a shut, unboarded window,
  breaking it open (glass noise, glass on the floor); a can or bottle does not.
- **Hits**: damage and a stagger; a baseball to the head (the arc at head height) knocks one down for 1.6 s. The one
  hit turns toward where the throw came from. Anything landing against an abandoned car jolts it and sets its alarm
  off (a bottle breaking within 2.5 m, as before).
- **Noise** where it lands, which the dead hear and come to: bottles break loud (`glass`, progression's
  `bottleNoise`), cans clatter (`cans`, 11 m), the rest thud (`thud`, 6–8 m).
- **After**: a bottle shatters into the field verbs' `glass:*` store (it crunches underfoot and is swept after 90 s);
  anything else lies where it stopped as an ordinary ground drop (`drop:t:*`) to pick up and throw again.

| Item | Range | Damage | On a hit | Noise | Windows |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Baseball | 20 m | 12 | bonk (knockdown 1.6 s) on the head, else stagger | thud 6 m | breaks |
| Brick | 11 m | 34 | stagger 0.9 s | thud 8 m | breaks |
| Rock | 15 m | 20 | stagger 0.7 s | thud 6 m | breaks |
| Tin can | 14 m | 3 | stagger 0.25 s | clatter 11 m | bounces off |
| Bottle | 12 m (`bottleRange`) | 8 | stagger 0.5 s | glass 15 m (`bottleNoise`) | shatters on it |

**Authority and co-op.** The wind-up is tracked per seat in the feature's state from `stepSurvivorMovement`, which
runs while predicting too, so a client's arc preview knows its own wind-up; only the room throws. Each throw is one
`toss:<k>` ledger store from a ring of 16 (start offset, impact offset, rest point, peak, flight time, outcome bits),
so every seat draws the same flight from `tossAt` with no new wire fields. The room lands each throw after its flight
(damage, window, noise) and leaves the drop after the roll. The only wire addition is the `thud` noise kind, appended
to the noise section's kind table. A false `fireHeld` does not survive the wire (flags carry only `true`), so a
release reads as `undefined` in the room; the wind-up treats both as released.

**Today.** Lab › Interactions › Throwables › Today (off): no throwables in the world and the bottle is the old instant
fixed-range throw (`progression.tossBottles`).

Tests: `games/outbreak/tests/interactions-throwables.test.ts`, `tests/interactions-drag.test.ts`, the bottle cases in `tests/verbs.test.ts`, and seat
parity for baseballs and bottles in `tests/coop-ledger-features.test.ts`.

## Drag and brace

Loose furniture: a chair or a dresser, and a mattress or a table, in most houses (up to two per house), on open floor
clear of the house's own furniture, walls and doorways, and 2 m clear in front of a closet so you can still get in
(`furniture.ts`, `furnitureSites`, seeded once per house as
`furn:<building>:<i>` ledger stores). The house's baked furniture stays put; these pieces are extra and drawn by the
interactions presenter (box-built, with a lying-down twin for when the dead have shoved one over).

- **E at a piece: Drag.** It goes square in front of you along your aim. You slow to the piece's share of walking
  pace (chair 0.85, mattress 0.75, table 0.7, dresser 0.55; Lab › Dragging speed) and cannot sprint. Other survivors
  bump into pieces; the one you drag does not block you. The piece is let go if you go down, die or get in a car.
- **E again: Set down,** where it is, or **Brace** when it is within 1.4 m of a door or window it can hold (a chair
  only wedges doors; tables, dressers and mattresses do either). Braced, it stands flush against the opening on your
  side, square to it, a door slams shut, and the crowd counts the opening as barricaded until the piece is gone:
  chair 70, mattress 110, table 150, dresser 240 hit points (Lab › Brace strength).
- **The dead bash** the planks off first, then the furniture (`PortalHolds.absorb`); at 0 it is shoved 0.7 m into the
  room and falls over, with a bang the dead hear. E on it again (Pull away / Drag) stands it up and takes hold.
- **Carrying a car battery** slows you to 0.85 of walking pace (Lab › Carrying a car battery; 1 is Today).

**The crowd's hook.** `OutbreakAISubsystem.portalHolds` (`shared/ai.ts`, `PortalHolds`): `held(id)` makes a door or
window count as one plank for navigation, hearing, open-door solids and bash targeting, and is part of the topology
digest; `absorb(id, damage)` takes bash damage once the planks are gone. The interactions feature installs it each
tick (`holdsFor`), keyed by braced store → portal id.

**Bots path round it.** `survivorObstacles` on shared features (`feature-registry.ts`): the interactions feature
lists every piece no one is dragging, and survivor bots add them to their local nav grid and steering blockers
(`BotWorldView.obstacles`), rebuilt when a piece is set down. Without it bots walked into chairs and stopped.

**Speed hook.** `movementScale` on shared features (`survivorMovementScale` in `feature-registry.ts`), applied to
walking speed in `stepSurvivor` and so predicted the same way on a co-op client.

## Hauling a downed teammate

A downed teammate's prompt is now `E Drag ◦Revive`: tap E takes them under the arms (`haul:<seat>` store) and they
trail 0.8 m behind you while you walk at 0.55 pace (Lab › Hauling speed); tap again (Let go) to put them down; hold E
still revives. The haul ends when either of you is gone, you go down or into a car, or they are back up or dead.
`toggleHaul` is called from the death feature's prompt (`shared/death/runtime.ts`).

## Boarding

Boarding up was already there (B nails one plank, up to three, at the door or window the prompt points at). Kit asked
for it again, so two rough edges are gone:

- **One B boards it up.** After a board goes up, the next starts on the same opening by itself, at its own noise,
  until there are three, the belt is out of planks or you walk off or sprint (which cancels a channel as before).
  With a crowbar in hand B still re-nails a damaged barricade and does not chain. `progression.chainBoards`, set from
  Lab › Interactions › Boarding › "One B boards it up" (Today: one board per press).
- **Hold E pries a board off** a boarded door or window, from either side: a 1.6 s channel (Lab › Verbs › Pry a board
  off, its noise 9 m), and the plank goes back in your belt. Before, a boarded door only said "Blocked by barricade"
  and you were shut in your own safehouse until the dead broke it. The tap is still refused, and its message now says
  "Boarded 2/3 · hold E to pry one off". A boarded window's tap (Peek) waits for the release, so the hold reaches the
  pry without peeking first. `shared/interactions/boards.ts` wraps the door and window handlers (`PRY_OFF`, the
  `pry` action with the crowbar glyph), and the ledger rule `unboard` does the work; `OutbreakAISubsystem.
  removeBarricadePlank` takes the plank and its share of the barricade's hit points. Lab › "Hold E pries a board off"
  (Today: boards stay).

## Teaching

The world prompt and training room belong to the onboarding pass (`docs/outbreak-onboarding.md`). The interactions
feature adds one in-world reminder line low over the survivor (`src/interactions/hint.ts`): with a throwable in hand,
the Mouse0 hold cap and "Throw · hold for distance", the ring filling as the throw winds up.

Boarding teaches itself in the door and window prompt: B Board up while there is room and a plank, and the Hold E
ring with the crowbar glyph (Pry off a board) once there is a board up.

Furniture and hauling use the world prompt (E with the `drag`, `set-down` and `brace` glyphs added to
`@arcade/kit/client/action-glyphs`), so they teach themselves where the prompt does.

## Sounds wanted (audio owns `src/audio`)

Dragging: a scrape loop while a `furn:*` store has `drag` and is moving; a thump when one braces (`br` 0→1); a crash
when one is shoved over (`down` 0→1). Throws: a whoosh on release scaled by power; landing thud per item (baseball on grass/wood, brick, rock, can
clatter/roll); a bonk on a head hit; glass for a window broken by a throw (the `glass:*` store already plays
`glass.break` for bottles).

## Clip

`bun scripts/interactions-clip.ts` (in `games/outbreak`; run it through `hivemind run --kind browser --fetch
captures/interactions-clip`) plays every staged scene with scripted input in headless, muted Chromium and writes JPEG
frames plus a readout of what each scene left behind (`SCENES=board,pry` for a subset). Each scene starts the survivor
on their feet at full health with empty hands and hangs Ash's front door back up if an earlier scene's dead tore it
off. Hauling is not in it: it needs a second seat.

## Considered and cut

- Pushing abandoned cars, or using one as a moving wall: the vehicles feature owns cars, and it is a bigger job.
- Curtains and blinds that block sight through a window: small, but the crowd's sight model has no hook for it yet.
- Kicking a door into the dead: doors and their breaches belong to AR-97.
- Throwing a chair or other furniture, and stacking several pieces against one opening: one braced piece per opening.
- Bots that throw, drag or pry on purpose: bots throw a bottle as before and path round furniture, nothing more.
